## 2b. Approval, Payment & Attachments workflows (deep dive)

This section completes the walkthrough of the "Approvals" and "Payments" guided tours (previously only summarized), including their mobile counterparts, plus what was found for Attachments.

### Approval workflows — desktop
- The `Approval ▾` nav item splits into two independent queues via a dropdown: **Invoices** and **PO Mismatches** — approvers pick which type of exception/document they're clearing, rather than one merged inbox.
- Starting approval is a **bulk action from the Invoices list itself**: select row checkbox(es) → `Approval ▾` menu → **Start Approval** / **Cancel Approval**. This confirms with a **"Start Approval Summary" modal**: a checklist-style confirmation ("✓ Started (1 of 1)") listing exactly which invoices were submitted, by Type/Vendor/Invoice Number/Amount, before letting the user close it. Bulk actions always show a scoped success receipt, not a generic toast.
- Once submitted, the approver's own view becomes a **personal "Ready to Approve" inbox** (View • Default = "Ready to Approve"), scoped to invoices assigned to them — this is a distinct saved view, not a filter the user has to build.
- Approving/rejecting from this inbox opens an **"Approve Invoices" modal**: an optional free-text **Comment** field, an **"Eligible for Approval (N of M)" status strip** (green dot) showing how many of the selected items actually qualify, a recap table (Type/Vendor/Invoice Number/Amount), and a single confiral button labelled with the exact count — **"Approve Invoices (1)"**. Bulk approval never hides the count behind a generic "Confirm."

### Approval workflows — mobile app
The tour includes a full **mobile app mockup** (phone frame, not just "responsive web"), presented as an equally first-class surface:
- **Home screen ("Welcome Back!")**: two large tappable summary cards — "Awaiting Your Approvals: 1 Invoice → Go to Approvals" and "No PO Mismatches → Go to PO Mismatch Approvals." Even with zero items in one queue, the empty queue still gets its own card and CTA (consistent presence, not a hidden empty state).
- **List screen ("Ready to Approve")**: each row is a card, not a table row — due date, a status pill ("In Progress"), amount in green, vendor name. Card-based density on mobile vs. table density on desktop — the same data, re-composed per surface rather than a squeezed-down table.
- **Detail screen**: a vertical field list (Doc Type, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, Bill Description, GL Account, Location, Department), a **"More From This Vendor"** section (surfaces vendor history/duplicate risk inline), and an **"Approval History"** section styled like a **package-tracking timeline** — a vertical line connecting circular step markers ("● INITIATED — Jessica Sadow, 5/1/2024 10:58 AM" → "○ PENDING") with avatar photos per actor. This timeline metaphor (borrowed from shipment tracking, not from typical enterprise software) makes a multi-step approval chain immediately scannable even to a non-technical mobile user.
- **Approval Context screen**: reachable by tapping "View" next to the amount — shows the actual invoice image thumbnail at the top, then the same field list, confirming the source-document-next-to-data pairing holds even on the small mobile surface, just stacked vertically instead of side-by-side.
- Fixed **bottom action bar** with large **Reject** (red) / **Approve** (green) buttons always visible while scrolling the detail — a thumb-reachable, unambiguous binary decision point.

=======
12-- **Row click does two things at once:** the row **expands in place** (Expenses / Items tabs, GL line table, `View PO` toggle, per-line Status labels, `Enter Manual Match Mode`) **and** a **right-hand source pane** (~490px ≈ 36%) opens with the PDF, zoom, page nav, Edit ▾, download, open-in-new-tab. The list stays on the left, columns narrowed.
13-- **Checkbox select opens Audit / Approval on the left** (~312px), replacing the View column. Audit is a flat log with "Refresh audit log"; Approval is STEP n → Rejected/Approved with named users, reason, and an INITIATED footer.
14:- **Batch detail (Payments) opens as a wide right sheet** (~1100px ≈ 78%) with a summary strip (submitted by, bills, total, bank) and a **sticky bottom action bar** (Reject / Approve & Pay). Same sticky bottom bar as the mobile approval screen.
15-- Per-cell confidence underline has **three** states in the PO view: green (confident), yellow (partial), grey (no prediction). Section 2 above only mentioned green.
16-- PO-backed invoices live on the **Invoices** queue with a `PO` badge on the Type chip (red numbered badge = mismatches). The Purchase Orders screen is only the imported PO list (Status, Type, Vendor, Buyer, PO Number, Amount, Currency, Created). Matching is resolved on the invoice row, not on the PO screen.
17-- Bill Pay rows: Terms (`2-10-30`), countdown badge (`Expires in N Days` / `N Days Away` / `N Days Overdue`), Est. Arrival Date with method, and **Amount To Pay with the discounted amount over the struck-through due amount** — the inline-adjustment pattern #188 generalised.
18-
19-**What this corrects in DocuBite's reading of Vic**
20-- #198's left-side History panel and #215's below-row expansion were both Vic-faithful. They failed in DocuBite because the work area was 800px, not because the placement was wrong.
21-- #211's eleven inline filter pills across two rows are not Vic's shape; Vic shows summary chips and a facet panel.
22-- Map #177's standing note that DocuBite keeps a *combined* fields+source pane (from #179) is the one deliberate departure; Vic splits fields (in-row) from source (right pane). #224 records the consequence: with a combined ~60% pane, History moves into that pane as tabs instead of a left panel.

## Resolution — 2026-09-15

Grilled in two rounds with `intent` (journey → fortify → articulate), `impeccable` (critique of the incumbent, then `shape`), `grilling` and `domain-modeling`. The user agreed every recommendation as put. Nothing here reverses a #177 decision; #185 (count-bearing modal, eligibility strip, receipt), #180 (`scopeToCurrentUser`), #192 (Exceptions), #224 (combined pane) are cited as-is.

### Critique of the incumbent (`/review`, `components/workspace/review-inbox.tsx`)

Dual-agent, snapshot `.impeccable/critique/2026-09-15T19-46-57Z__components-workspace-review-inbox-tsx.md`. **21/40.** In-page `detect.js`: list **12 / 6**, row selected **17 / 9** (1440 / 390); static scan 0. Design specificity: generic. Priority issues: **P0** the mobile sheet's Approve/Reject bar paints under the app's bottom nav (`review-inbox.tsx:750` vs `mobile-tab-bar.tsx:36`) — untappable; **P1** approve gate checks only Paid/Unpaid, so a failed duplicate check still gets an enabled Approve; **P1** optimistic approval where CONTEXT.md says Server-confirmed; **P1** amount renders "—" on every row; **P1** a second grammar for the job the Queue screen now does.

The finding that reframed the ticket: **`ReviewTask` is not an approval.** All eight creation sites (`document-checks.ts:220`, `automation-rules.ts:133–285`, `integration-push.ts:107`, `readiness/refresh.ts:301`, `document-matches.ts:81`) create it workflow-less for review reasons; a workflow only attaches by hand. Today's inbox mixes *review* (operator fixes) with *approval* (approver decides).

### Decisions

1. **A row of Approvals › Invoices is a submitted Approval** — a `ReviewTask` with a workflow at a stage. Workflow-less tasks are not an inbox; they are why an invoice shows *In review* / *Needs attention* on Invoices under `Approval · Not started`. `/review` and `/review/[taskId]` 308 to `/approvals/invoices[/documentId]`.
2. **"Assigned to me" = `canDecideStage(currentStage, myRole, myId)`**, surfaced as the system view **Ready to Approve** with `scopeToCurrentUser: true` (#180's flag gets its purpose). `assigneeId` stays "who works a review"; it does not gate approvals.
3. **A row of Approvals › PO Mismatches is a `match-variance` Gate in `blocked`**, one per invoice. Approve = `overrideGate(reason)` (attributed, audited, clears the gate as #184's Override Mode does); Reject rejects the invoice's Approval. `DocumentMatch` pending is a matching question (#228); `po_line_consumption` failures escalate to Exceptions (#192).
4. **PO Mismatch rows appear automatically** when the gate fires on an invoice with a decidable stage; no second Start. The approver is the current stage's approver until Admin's PO Mismatch Flows (#231) can name another.
5. **Open Exception or failed hard check → row stays in Ready to Approve as *Not eligible***, reason on the row, Approve disabled with visible text (not `title`), eligibility strip per #185 ("1 of 3 not eligible: open exception"). Never hidden, never overridable from Approvals. This fixes the P1 gate bug by design.
6. **Same Detail pane, three approver differences**: opens on the **Approval** tab (STEP n → who/when/reason, INITIATED footer); extracted fields **read-only** while a stage is pending; sticky footer **Reject · Approve** through the #185 modal, **Send back for review** in the header overflow.
7. **Start Approval lives on the Invoices bulk bar** (Approval ▾ → Start / Cancel) with the Start Approval Summary receipt. A **workspace default workflow that auto-starts** on In review with no blocking check is a new Admin setting (handed to #231); until it exists, manual Start only. SMB (#78): the owner starts and approves, one stage, "Approve as signer of record" survives.
8. **Columns.** Invoices: Processing mark · Supplier · Invoice # · Amount · Due · Stage ("2 of 3 · Owner sign-off") · Waiting since. PO Mismatches: mark · Supplier · Invoice # · PO # · Variance (amount and %, tolerance beside it) · Stage. Header: one band, View picker = the two queues (with counts), chips `Status · Ready to approve` · `Approver · Me`, no tabs. Decision bar: sticky pane footer for the selected row + bulk bar Approve/Reject for a multi-select, one action, two entry points, same modal.
9. **Rail**: after Exceptions, before Worksheets; badge = my Ready to Approve count across both queues, never the workspace-wide count (Attention Bait, catalog cat. 5).
10. **State inventory** (execution checklist): nothing for me · nothing for me but pending on others (offer `Approver · Anyone`) · ineligible only · loading (62px skeletons) · **decision in flight: row stays, footer pending, leaves only on the server's answer, no optimistic removal, no Undo** · server refused (inline, "Approved by Dana 12s ago", row refreshes) · partial bulk (#185 receipt per row) · no workflow configured (Start explains and links to Admin › Approval Flows) · approver no longer a member (*Needs attention · no approver*, owner decides) · offline (buttons disabled with the reason, list readable).
11. **Reject requires a free-text reason**; so does the PO-mismatch Approve (it is an override). Plain Approve keeps Vic's optional Comment. No reason picklist.
12. **Approval never publishes by itself.** The last stage sets *Approved*; the ledger push stays a separate visible action (#229). Modal copy names the consequence honestly; if an auto-push rule exists it is named.
13. **Words** added to CONTEXT.md: Approval, Approver, Ready to Approve, Send back for review, Not eligible; Work item narrowed. Retired from the UI: "Review queue", "Reason: Rule required / Check failed", "Reopen", `in_review` as a pickable status.
14. **Mobile**: this ticket decides content, #232 decides composition (card · stacked Approval Context · timeline · fixed bar above the nav). The P0 z-index defect is fixed in this ticket's execution because the below-`lg` sheet is the same component.
15. **Keyboard**: inherits the queue's ↑/↓/Escape/Enter, adds nothing. **No single-key approve** (`e` is Destructive Defaults, cat. 9). Closes the shortcuts fog for Approvals only.
16. **Routes/code**: `review-inbox.tsx` and the orphaned `review-task-detail.tsx` are deleted, not adapted; the push receipt is lifted into the queue's actions; approve-undo is not.

### Action Summary for the execution ticket (in order)

Intent: `specify` (spec + copy matrix + test plan from the decisions above) → `fortify` (the state inventory in decision 10 must exist in code before the happy path is called done) → `articulate` (modal, reason, eligibility, empty-state copy) → `include` (focus into the pane on open, `aria-current` on the row, `role="dialog"` on the sheet, footer reachable by Tab).
Impeccable: `shape` → `layout` (two queues on the #225 shell, Stage/Variance columns, footer + bulk bar) → `clarify` → `harden` (Server-confirmed in-flight and refusal states, offline) → `adapt` (390 sheet, bar above the nav) → `audit` → `polish`.
Definition of done: in-page `detect.js` on both queues at 1440 and 390, list and pane-open, before/after counts on the ticket (before: 12/6 · 17/9 on the incumbent); critique re-run must beat 21/40; `evaluate` score recorded; `craft-floor.md` read before the first edit.

Priority issues: **P0** the mobile sheet's Approve/Reject bar paints under the app's bottom nav (`review-inbox.tsx:750` vs `mobile-tab-bar.tsx:36`) — untappable; **P1** approve gate checks only Paid/Unpaid, so a failed duplicate check still gets an enabled Approve; **P1** optimistic approval where CONTEXT.md says Server-confirmed; **P1** amount renders "—" on every row; **P1** a second grammar for the job the Queue screen now does.

The finding that reframed the ticket: **`ReviewTask` is not an approval.** All eight creation sites (`document-checks.ts:220`, `automation-rules.ts:133–285`, `integration-push.ts:107`, `readiness/refresh.ts:301`, `document-matches.ts:81`) create it workflow-less for review reasons; a workflow only attaches by hand. Today's inbox mixes *review* (operator fixes) with *approval* (approver decides).

### Decisions

1. **A row of Approvals › Invoices is a submitted Approval** — a `ReviewTask` with a workflow at a stage. Workflow-less tasks are not an inbox; they are why an invoice shows *In review* / *Needs attention* on Invoices under `Approval · Not started`. `/review` and `/review/[taskId]` 308 to `/approvals/invoices[/documentId]`.
2. **"Assigned to me" = `canDecideStage(currentStage, myRole, myId)`**, surfaced as the system view **Ready to Approve** with `scopeToCurrentUser: true` (#180's flag gets its purpose). `assigneeId` stays "who works a review"; it does not gate approvals.
3. **A row of Approvals › PO Mismatches is a `match-variance` Gate in `blocked`**, one per invoice. Approve = `overrideGate(reason)` (attributed, audited, clears the gate as #184's Override Mode does); Reject rejects the invoice's Approval. `DocumentMatch` pending is a matching question (#228); `po_line_consumption` failures escalate to Exceptions (#192).
4. **PO Mismatch rows appear automatically** when the gate fires on an invoice with a decidable stage; no second Start. The approver is the current stage's approver until Admin's PO Mismatch Flows (#231) can name another.
5. **Open Exception or failed hard check → row stays in Ready to Approve as *Not eligible***, reason on the row, Approve disabled with visible text (not `title`), eligibility strip per #185 ("1 of 3 not eligible: open exception"). Never hidden, never overridable from Approvals. This fixes the P1 gate bug by design.
6. **Same Detail pane, three approver differences**: opens on the **Approval** tab (STEP n → who/when/reason, INITIATED footer); extracted fields **read-only** while a stage is pending; sticky footer **Reject · Approve** through the #185 modal, **Send back for review** in the header overflow.
7. **Start Approval lives on the Invoices bulk bar** (Approval ▾ → Start / Cancel) with the Start Approval Summary receipt. A **workspace default workflow that auto-starts** on In review with no blocking check is a new Admin setting (handed to #231); until it exists, manual Start only. SMB (#78): the owner starts and approves, one stage, "Approve as signer of record" survives.
8. **Columns.** Invoices: Processing mark · Supplier · Invoice # · Amount · Due · Stage ("2 of 3 · Owner sign-off") · Waiting since. PO Mismatches: mark · Supplier · Invoice # · PO # · Variance (amount and %, tolerance beside it) · Stage. Header: one band, View picker = the two queues (with counts), chips `Status · Ready to approve` · `Approver · Me`, no tabs. Decision bar: sticky pane footer for the selected row + bulk bar Approve/Reject for a multi-select, one action, two entry points, same modal.
9. **Rail**: after Exceptions, before Worksheets; badge = my Ready to Approve count across both queues, never the workspace-wide count (Attention Bait, catalog cat. 5).
10. **State inventory** (execution checklist): nothing for me · nothing for me but pending on others (offer `Approver · Anyone`) · ineligible only · loading (62px skeletons) · **decision in flight: row stays, footer pending, leaves only on the server's answer, no optimistic removal, no Undo** · server refused (inline, "Approved by Dana 12s ago", row refreshes) · partial bulk (#185 receipt per row) · no workflow configured (Start explains and links to Admin › Approval Flows) · approver no longer a member (*Needs attention · no approver*, owner decides) · offline (buttons disabled with the reason, list readable).
11. **Reject requires a free-text reason**; so does the PO-mismatch Approve (it is an override). Plain Approve keeps Vic's optional Comment. No reason picklist.
12. **Approval never publishes by itself.** The last stage sets *Approved*; the ledger push stays a separate visible action (#229). Modal copy names the consequence honestly; if an auto-push rule exists it is named.
13. **Words** added to CONTEXT.md: Approval, Approver, Ready to Approve, Send back for review, Not eligible; Work item narrowed. Retired from the UI: "Review queue", "Reason: Rule required / Check failed", "Reopen", `in_review` as a pickable status.
14. **Mobile**: this ticket decides content, #232 decides composition (card · stacked Approval Context · timeline · fixed bar above the nav). The P0 z-index defect is fixed in this ticket's execution because the below-`lg` sheet is the same component.
15. **Keyboard**: inherits the queue's ↑/↓/Escape/Enter, adds nothing. **No single-key approve** (`e` is Destructive Defaults, cat. 9). Closes the shortcuts fog for Approvals only.
16. **Routes/code**: `review-inbox.tsx` and the orphaned `review-task-detail.tsx` are deleted, not adapted; the push receipt is lifted into the queue's actions; approve-undo is not.

### Action Summary for the execution ticket (in order)

Intent: `specify` (spec + copy matrix + test plan from the decisions above) → `fortify` (the state inventory in decision 10 must exist in code before the happy path is called done) → `articulate` (modal, reason, eligibility, empty-state copy) → `include` (focus into the pane on open, `aria-current` on the row, `role="dialog"` on the sheet, footer reachable by Tab).
Impeccable: `shape` → `layout` (two queues on the #225 shell, Stage/Variance columns, footer + bulk bar) → `clarify` → `harden` (Server-confirmed in-flight and refusal states, offline) → `adapt` (390 sheet, bar above the nav) → `audit` → `polish`.
Definition of done: in-page `detect.js` on both queues at 1440 and 390, list and pane-open, before/after counts on the ticket (before: 12/6 · 17/9 on the incumbent); critique re-run must beat 21/40; `evaluate` score recorded; `craft-floor.md` read before the first edit.

content.content:
> **Additional context needed**: target platforms/devices and usage contexts.

Adapt an existing design to a different context: another screen size, device, platform, or use case. The trap is treating adaptation as scaling. The job is rethinking the experience for the new context.

**Web only** (mobile web included). Native platforms (`ios` / `android` / `adaptive`) route to [adapt.native.md](adapt.native.md) instead; if the project is native, switch to it now.

---

## Assess Adaptation Challenge

Understand what needs adaptation and why:

1. **Identify the source context**:
   - What was it designed for originally? (Desktop web? Mobile app?)
   - What assumptions were made? (Large screen? Mouse input? Fast connection?)
   - What works well in current context?

2. **Understand target context**:
   - **Device**: Mobile, tablet, desktop, TV, watch, print?
   - **Input method**: Touch, mouse, keyboard, voice, gamepad?
   - **Screen constraints**: Size, resolution, orientation?
   - **Connection**: Fast wifi, slow 3G, offline?
   - **Usage context**: On-the-go vs desk, quick glance vs focused reading?
   - **User expectations**: What do users expect on this platform?

3. **Identify adaptation challenges**:
   - What won't fit? (Content, navigation, features)
   - What won't work? (Hover states on touch, tiny touch targets)
   - What's inappropriate? (Desktop patterns on mobile, mobile patterns on desktop)

**CRITICAL**: Adaptation is rethinking the experience for the new context, not scaling pixels.

## Plan Adaptation Strategy

Create context-appropriate strategy:

### Mobile Adaptation (Desktop → Mobile)

**Layout Strategy**:
- Single column instead of multi-column
- Vertical stacking instead of side-by-side
- Full-width components instead of fixed widths
- Bottom navigation instead of top/side navigation

**Interaction Strategy**:
- Touch targets 44x44px minimum (not hover-dependent)
- Swipe gestures where appropriate (lists, carousels)
- Bottom sheets instead of dropdowns
- Thumbs-first design (controls within thumb reach)
- Larger tap areas with more spacing

**Content Strategy**:
- Progressive disclosure (don't show everything at once)
- Prioritize primary content (secondary content in tabs/accordions)
- Shorter text (more concise)
- Larger text (16px minimum)

**Navigation Strategy**:
- Hamburger menu or bottom navigation
- Reduce navigation complexity
- Sticky headers for context
- Back button in navigation flow

### Tablet Adaptation (Hybrid Approach)

**Layout Strategy**:
- Two-column layouts (not single or three-column)
- Side panels for secondary content
- Master-detail views (list + detail)
- Adaptive based on orientation (portrait vs landscape)

**Interaction Strategy**:
- Support both touch and pointer
- Touch targets 44x44px but allow denser layouts than phone
- Side navigation drawers
- Multi-column forms where appropriate

### Desktop Adaptation (Mobile → Desktop)

**Layout Strategy**:
- Multi-column layouts (use horizontal space)
- Side navigation always visible
- Multiple information panels simultaneously
- Fixed widths with max-width constraints (don't stretch to 4K)

**Interaction Strategy**:
- Hover states for additional information
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Right-click context menus
- Drag and drop where helpful
- Multi-select with Shift/Cmd

**Content Strategy**:
- Show more information upfront (less progressive disclosure)
- Data tables with many columns
- Richer visualizations
- More detailed descriptions

### Print Adaptation (Screen → Print)

**Layout Strategy**:
- Page breaks at logical points
- Remove navigation, footer, interactive elements
- Black and white (or limited color)
- Proper margins for binding

**Content Strategy**:
- Expand shortened content (show full URLs, hidden sections)
- Add page numbers, headers, footers
- Include metadata (print date, page title)
- Convert charts to print-friendly versions

### Email Adaptation (Web → Email)

**Layout Strategy**:
- Narrow width (600px max)
- Single column only
- Inline CSS (no external stylesheets)
- Table-based layouts (for email client compatibility)

content.content: Launching skill: grilling

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/ubuntu/Dev/Wes-doc/.claude/skills/grilling

Interview the user relentlessly until you reach a shared understanding. Map this as a **design tree**: every decision branches into the decisions that hang off it.

Work the tree in **rounds**. The **frontier** is every decision whose prerequisites are already settled: the questions you can ask _now_ without guessing at answers you haven't heard yet. Ask the whole frontier in one round: number each question and give your recommended answer. Then wait for the user's answers before the next round.

Format a round like so:

```
❓ **Q1** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>

---

❓ **Q2** - **<question title>**: <question body, might be multiple paragraphs, including multiple choices>

➡️ <your recommended answer>
```

Each round the user answers reshapes the tree: settled decisions push the frontier outward and unblock questions that depended on them. Recompute the frontier and ask the next round. A question whose answer depends on another question still open in this round belongs to a _later_ round, not this one.

Finding _facts_ is your job, never the user's. When a frontier question needs a fact from the environment (filesystem, tools, etc.), dispatch a sub-agent to find it; don't ask the user for anything you could look up yourself. Don't block on it: a running exploration is an unsettled prerequisite, so only the questions downstream of it wait for the sub-agent to report; ask the rest of the frontier now. The _decisions_ are the user's: put each to them and wait.

The session is done when the frontier is empty: every branch of the design tree visited, nothing left silently assumed. Do not act on it until the user confirms you have reached a shared understanding.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /home/ubuntu/Dev/Wes-doc/.claude/skills/domain-modeling

# Domain Modeling

Actively build and sharpen the project's domain model as you design. This is the *active* discipline: challenging terms, inventing edge-case scenarios, and writing the glossary and decisions down the moment they crystallise. (Merely *reading* `CONTEXT.md` for vocabulary is not this skill: that's a one-line habit any skill can do. This skill is for when you're changing the model, not just consuming it.)

## File structure

Most repos have a single context:

```
/
├── CONTEXT.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/
│       ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md
│       └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md
└── src/
```

If a `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists at the root, the repo has multiple contexts. The map points to where each one lives:

```
/
├── CONTEXT-MAP.md
├── docs/
│   └── adr/                          ← system-wide decisions
├── src/
│   ├── ordering/
│   │   ├── CONTEXT.md
│   │   └── docs/adr/                 ← context-specific decisions
│   └── billing/
│       ├── CONTEXT.md
│       └── docs/adr/
```

Create files lazily: only when you have something to write. If no `CONTEXT.md` exists, create one when the first term is resolved. If no `docs/adr/` exists, create it when the first ADR is needed.

## During the session

### Challenge against the glossary

When the user uses a term that conflicts with the existing language in `CONTEXT.md`, call it out immediately. "Your glossary defines 'cancellation' as X, but you seem to mean Y. Which is it?"

### Sharpen fuzzy language

When the user uses vague or overloaded terms, propose a precise canonical term. "You're saying 'account': do you mean the Customer or the User? Those are different things."

### Discuss concrete scenarios

When domain relationships are being discussed, stress-test them with specific scenarios. Invent scenarios that probe edge cases and force the user to be precise about the boundaries between concepts.

### Cross-reference with code

When the user states how something works, check whether the code agrees. If you find a contradiction, surface it: "Your code cancels entire Orders, but you just said partial cancellation is possible. Which is right?"

### Update CONTEXT.md inline

When a term is resolved, update `CONTEXT.md` right there. Don't batch these up: capture them as they happen. Use the format in [CONTEXT-FORMAT.md](./CONTEXT-FORMAT.md).

`CONTEXT.md` should be totally devoid of implementation details. Do not treat `CONTEXT.md` as a spec, a scratch pad, or a repository for implementation decisions. It is a glossary and nothing else.

### Offer ADRs sparingly

Only offer to create an ADR when all three are true:

1. **Hard to reverse**: the cost of changing your mind later is meaningful
2. **Surprising without context**: a future reader will wonder "why did they do it this way?"
3. **The result of a real trade-off**: there were genuine alternatives and you picked one for specific reasons

If any of the three is missing, skip the ADR. Use the format in [ADR-FORMAT.md](./ADR-FORMAT.md).

## Context (Intent, established once)

- **User**: the **Approver** (CONTEXT.md) — a stage's named approver or any owner — deciding on a phone between other work. Behaviour: opens the app by habit (no notification yet, #246), wants "what needs me", reads one invoice, decides, leaves. Assumed, not researched (PRODUCT.md, `docs/journeys/operator-working-day.md` Q7).
- **Constraints**: thumb reach, interruption, glare, slow/absent connection, no keyboard; a decision is Server-confirmed with no Undo (#227 §10), so mis-taps are the costliest failure.
- **Ethical stance**: no attention bait (badge = *my* Ready to Approve only, #227 §9), no single-gesture approve (Destructive Defaults, cat. 9), no optimistic state.
- **Success**: an Approver clears Ready to Approve on a phone without opening a laptop; zero decisions taken by accident; state always honest.
- **Impeccable mode**: **Operate**, phone. Incumbent visual truth: `detail-pane.tsx` (fixed `inset-0 z-50` sheet below `lg`, Back, sticky footer), `split-pane.tsx` (source 38vh stacked over fields when embedded), `mobile-tab-bar.tsx` (4 slots, `z-40`), `review-inbox.tsx` mobile cards + bar (being deleted, #227 §16).
- **Incumbent critique, cited not re-run** (the old inbox is replaced, not refined): #227's critique of the mobile inbox 21/40, in-page 12/6 · 17/9; P0 decision bar painting under the tab bar; P1 optimistic approval; P1 "—" amounts; second grammar. #225's Invoices sheet at 390: 6/5 pane-open.

## Round 1 — user, landing, flow, IA

❓ **Q1 – Phone landing**: Vic's two-card "Welcome back" home, the Invoices queue (status quo since #237), or Ready to Approve?

➡️ **Invoices stays the landing on every width; Approvals is the first tab.** CONTEXT.md "Workspace home: no separate overview surface" (#237) is a documented decision, so Vic's card home does not win the tie; a viewport-sniffing redirect to Approvals is the least reversible option. The cards' one virtue — the empty queue stays present — is delivered by Q4's segmented View picker showing both counts. Rule: map Notes → CONTEXT.md → smallest reversible.

❓ **Q2 – Tab bar**: what replaces the interim Invoices · Exceptions · Finance-or-Archive · Settings?

➡️ **Approvals · Invoices · Exceptions · Account.** Approvals first because the phone is the Approver's lane (#239 Q7); Account per #231. Finance is off the daily route and Archive is a lookup side-path (#239), so neither earns a thumb slot; the Account screen carries an "Also in this workspace" link list (Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Archive, Finance — all read-only on the phone, content-only when deep-linked, like Admin). Badges: Approvals = my Ready to Approve count, Exceptions = open count, **Invoices loses its badge** (today's `pipelineReviewCount` is workspace-wide review work — Attention Bait, cat. 5, on the lane the phone doesn't serve).

❓ **Q3 – Nothing to approve / not an approver**: what does the Approvals tab show?

➡️ The "done" empty state (#239): "Nothing needs your approval", then the honest secondary line "N waiting on other approvers" with the `Approver · Anyone` chip (#227 §10), and a link to Invoices. Never hidden, never a dead end (cat. 9).

❓ **Q4 – Two queues on a phone**: Vic has two cards → two lists. DocuBite's Approvals is one destination with a View picker.

➡️ One list screen titled **Ready to Approve** with a **segmented control Invoices (n) · PO Mismatches (n)** under the header — both counts always visible, even at zero. Sort and facet chips collapse into one **Filter** button opening a bottom sheet (Vic's facet panel re-composed; evidence: #225's chips wrap to three rows at 390).

❓ **Q5 – Row anatomy**: Vic's card: due date, status pill, amount in green, vendor.

➡️ A tappable card, ≥64px, processing mark at the leading edge (#223): line 1 Supplier (15px semibold) · Amount (tabular, right); line 2 Invoice # · Due; line 3 Stage "2 of 3 · Owner sign-off" or the **Not eligible** reason pill. PO Mismatches swaps line 2 for PO # · Variance (amount, %). Amount in DocuBite's ink, not green — colour carries state only (no colour-only meaning; #233 one status vocabulary). No checkboxes below `lg`: **bulk is desktop-only**; one row, one decision on a phone (Destructive Defaults).

❓ **Q6 – Detail vs Approval Context**: Vic has two mobile screens (field list + timeline; then "View" → image + fields). DocuBite's pane is combined fields+source (documented exception, #224).

➡️ **One sheet, not two screens.** The below-`lg` Detail pane *is* the phone sheet: source strip (38vh, collapsible to a "Show source" bar) above tabs **Approval · Details · Checks · History**, opening on Approval (#227 §6), fields read-only while a stage is pending. Vic's "View → Approval Context" collapses into expanding the source strip. Rule: documented exception to Vic.

❓ **Q7 – Timeline**: package-tracking timeline with avatars, or #227's STEP n list?

➡️ **Same component on both widths**: vertical timeline, one node per stage — decided (name, when, reason), current ("Waiting on you" / "Waiting on Dana"), not reached — with an avatar (`User.avatar` when set, initials otherwise), INITIATED as the first node. #227 §6's STEP n → who/when/reason is this list; #209 already built the mobile version. Vic wins the tie on form; one component keeps #233's vocabulary.

❓ **Q8 – More From This Vendor**: fog said "needs the supplier model checked".

➡️ **Build it from existing data, no new model**: a "From this supplier" line on the Approval tab — `Supplier.documentCount`, `lastSeenAt`, terms (`paymentTermsDays`, #229's discount) — plus the near-duplicate check (`lib/checks/duplicates.ts`) as "Possible duplicate of INV-… · opened" when it fired. On both widths (one pane). Graduates the fog item. Principle: evidence in view before a decision (#228's "arithmetic in view").

❓ **Q9 – PO Mismatches on a phone**: #189 kept line matching desktop-only.

➡️ Approve stays `overrideGate(reason)` with the reason sheet; the phone shows the **variance summary** (Total ordered · invoiced · this invoice · over by · tolerance, #228's breakdown) read-only, and "Match lines on desktop" as a note, not a button. Per-cell glyphs remain desktop (#189, #228).

## Round 2 — behaviour, states, words, rendering, a11y

❓ **Q10 – Decision bar**: placement, size, order.

➡️ Sticky footer of the sheet, **Reject (outline, red-700 text) · Approve (filled emerald-700)**, two equal halves, 48px tall, safe-area padding; the sheet is `z-50` over the `z-40` tab bar so the bar is the bottom-most element (fixes #227's P0 by construction). Reject opens a bottom sheet with the required reason; Approve opens #185's count-bearing modal as a bottom sheet with optional comment. No swipe gestures.

❓ **Q11 – After a decision**: auto-advance, return to list, or stay?

➡️ **Stay on the row** (#239): footer shows "Approving…" (disabled, server-confirmed), then the result inline with "Next to approve" and "Back to list" — no auto-advance (autonomy; an interrupted Approver must not find the *next* invoice under their thumb).

❓ **Q12 – History and hardware Back**: desktop uses `replaceState`.

➡️ Below `lg`, opening a row **pushes** history so Android/iOS Back closes the sheet; ↑/↓ inside the sheet still replace. Real conditions: the system Back is the phone's Escape.

❓ **Q13 – Offline / refused / stale**: the phone hits these more.

➡️ #227 §10's inventory verbatim, phone-specific rendering: offline → both buttons disabled with "You're offline — decisions need a connection", list stays readable; server refused → inline "Approved by Dana 12s ago", row refreshes; Not eligible → Approve disabled with the reason as visible text above the bar, Reject stays enabled; loading → 64px card skeletons.

❓ **Q14 – Words**: tab label, sheet title, empty states.

➡️ Tab "Approvals" (the view is "Ready to Approve" — too long for a tab); sheet title = supplier, subtitle invoice # · amount; buttons "Reject" / "Approve" (modal confirms "Approve invoice"); "Waiting on you" not "In Progress" (#233); Not eligible reason in plain words ("Open exception: duplicate suspected").

❓ **Q15 – Type, spacing, colour at 390**: craft floor.

➡️ Card title 15px/600, secondary 13px/400 slate-600 (≥4.5:1), amounts `tabular-nums`; inputs 16px (iOS zoom); 16px horizontal gutter; hairlines slate-200; emerald only on the primary action and current node; red only on Reject and rejected nodes. `craft-floor.md` is missing from the repo (noted by #236) — its floor is applied from the `impeccable` skill's own reference.

❓ **Q16 – Motion**: sheet and result.

➡️ Sheet slides in from the right, 200ms ease-out, `prefers-reduced-motion` → instant; decision result crossfades 150ms; no bounce. Motion conveys "you went deeper; Back returns" (Intent decides it exists, Impeccable its form).

❓ **Q17 – Accessibility**: sheet and bar.

➡️ Sheet `role="dialog" aria-modal="true"`, focus to the heading on open, Back first in tab order, footer reachable by Tab; segmented control as a `tablist`; decision result in an `aria-live="polite"` region; 48px targets; no colour-only state (`include`).

❓ **Q18 – Tablet band (`md`–`lg`)**: tab bar hidden, rail shown, sheet full-screen.

➡️ Keep: the rail carries Approvals between 768 and 1023; the full-screen sheet applies. The tab-bar decision is `<md`; the sheet decision is `<lg`. Nothing to change; recorded so #235 and execution don't re-derive it.

❓ **Q19 – Success measure**: `measure`.

➡️ Share of Approval decisions taken below `lg`; time from Start to decision; counter-metric: reject-then-cancel and approve-modal-dismiss rates (mis-taps), and decisions/minute must not spike (rubber-stamping). Recorded, instrumentation not built.

# TaxHacker Product Context

This glossary defines the product language used for the authenticated workspace experience and its document-to-ledger workflow.

## Authenticated workspace experience

**Workspace home**:
The Invoices queue. Opening a workspace lands the user on their work, not on a summary of it; "what needs me" is read from the rail badges and the queue's own counts. There is no separate overview surface.
_Avoid_: Dashboard, landing page, overview, next best action

**Unplugged surface**:
A feature the product no longer shows or routes to, kept only so it can be brought back deliberately. Worksheets, Expenses and Dictation are unplugged. An unplugged surface has no navigation entry, no row or bulk action, no badge, and its addresses do not open.
_Avoid_: Hidden, deprecated, legacy

**Core workflow destinations**:
Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Finance, and Archive: the permission-filtered peer surfaces representing typed intake, escalated work, booked outcome, and the permanent source record. The four typed intake destinations replace the former single "Documents" surface.

**Document**:
The storage-and-extraction primitive underlying every typed destination. Every Invoice, Purchase Order, Receipt, and Bank Statement is a Document, but "Document" is no longer itself a user-facing destination — the user asserts which typed destination a Document belongs to at upload time, and that assertion is authoritative.
_Avoid_: Using "Document" as a destination name; unclassified/pending-classification states

**Invoice**:
The typed destination for a bill received from a supplier. Absorbs the former Documents/Bills surface; aging is a filter chip and a saved view here, and paying an approved invoice happens on Bill Pay, not on this queue.

**Purchase Order**:
The typed destination for a purchase order, paired with Invoices for matching and cumulative line-item comparison against what has already been invoiced against it.

**Receipt**:
The typed destination for a receipt. Absorbs expense-claim creation and approval as an action on selected rows rather than as its own destination.

**Bank Statement**:
The typed destination for a bank statement. The reviewer asserts the issuing institution; the first statement for that institution becomes its saved layout, and later uploads are checked against it for drift.

**Check**:
A tri-valued (pass/warn/fail), explainable comparison that states in plain language why a value is flagged, anchored to the field, cell, or row it concerns. "Mismatch" names one Check status, not the category.
_Avoid_: Discrepancy, issue, error (as the umbrella term)

**Line match**:
An invoice line's assigned Purchase Order line — guessed by description similarity, or set by hand in Match manually. A line below the similarity threshold has no line match and is not compared.
_Avoid_: Line pairing, line mapping

**Match manually**:
The named in-row mode on an invoice's line items that confirms, replaces or rejects its Purchase Order and reassigns line matches; the checks re-run when it is left. It changes the facts and needs no reason; it is not Override Mode, which accepts a variance with a reason.
_Avoid_: Manual Match Mode (Vic's name), re-match, Override (for a match change)

**Override Mode**:
The screen-scoped mode in which a soft check or gate can be overridden, each override attributed and recorded with a required reason. Hard gates are out of its reach.
_Avoid_: Bypass, force approve

**Fully invoiced**:
A Purchase Order whose every line has been invoiced to at least its ordered quantity. Derived, never set by hand.
_Avoid_: Closed PO, consumed

**Saved view**:
A named, reusable filter/sort/column configuration on a list screen. System views are seeded per screen and are not editable or deletable; a user can duplicate one into an editable, optionally shared, view.

**Work item**:
A single unit of pending work surfaced in a Next-action queue — a document awaiting review or a match awaiting confirmation. An approval awaiting a decision is an Approval, not a work item; it is worked by an Approver, not an assignee.

**Approval**:
A run started on an invoice by a person, moving through the stages of an approval flow until it is approved, rejected, or sent back for review. An invoice nobody has started an approval on is under review, not awaiting approval.
_Avoid_: Review task (the storage record), sign-off (as the umbrella term)

**Approver**:
The person who can decide the current stage of an Approval — a stage's named approver, or any owner where the stage names nobody. Distinct from an assignee, who works a review.
_Avoid_: Reviewer (that is who prepares the row), assignee

**Ready to Approve**:
The personal system view on the Approvals destination: every Approval whose current stage the signed-in person can decide, including rows that are not yet eligible, shown with the reason. The badge on the rail counts this view and nothing else.
_Avoid_: Pending approvals (that is the workspace-wide count), inbox

**Send back for review**:
The reversible middle path on an Approval: the stage is not decided, the invoice returns to review with a required reason, and the run can be restarted. Reject ends the run.
_Avoid_: Reopen, cancel (that withdraws a run before any stage is decided)

**Not eligible**:
An Approval that is visible to its Approver but cannot be decided yet because a hard check failed or an escalation is open on the invoice. Never hidden, never overridable from Approvals; the reason is shown on the row.

**Bill Pay**:
The queue of approved, unpaid invoices from which payment batches are created. An invoice reaches it only once its processing state is Approved; one that cannot be paid yet (no supplier bank details) stays visible with the reason.
_Avoid_: Payables, payment run (the queue), pay list

**Payment batch**:
A named set of approved invoices, one payer account and one currency, submitted by a member for an owner's decision. Pending approval, then Approved (its payment file can be downloaded), then Paid; or Rejected with a reason. Whether the file has been downloaded is a fact shown on the batch, not a state. A batch never moves money.
_Avoid_: Payment run, remittance (that is the advice sent to the supplier), transfer

**Payer account**:
A named workspace bank account a payment batch is to be paid from — a label that tells the uploader which bank portal the file belongs to. DocuBite never holds the account's credentials and the file never carries its number.
_Avoid_: Pay From (Vic's column label is fine on screen; the concept is the payer account), funding source, bank connection

**Payment terms**:
A supplier's net days and, when offered, an early-payment discount: the percent and the days within which it applies, shown as "2/10 net 30". A supplier without a discount shows no discount claim and no discount countdown.
_Avoid_: Terms code, "2-10-30"

**Payment record**:
A DocuBite-side fact that an amount was paid against an invoice on a date, by a batch or by hand (Mark as paid). An invoice's paid state is derived from the ledger when it confirms payment, otherwise from its payment records. A payment record can be removed with a reason.
_Avoid_: Mark as paid (the action, not the record), settlement, ledger payment (that is the ledger's own line)

**Company**:
The user-facing name for a team workspace in Admin and the switcher: one legal or financial entity with its own currency, tax jurisdiction, suppliers, ledger and members. "Workspace" remains the storage and address term. The auto-created personal workspace is shown as Personal, never as a company.
_Avoid_: Entity (Vic's word), tenant, client (that is who the company belongs to)

**Organization**:
A named group of companies an accountant or finance team runs under one login. Belonging to an organization never by itself opens any of its companies; access to each company is granted separately, with its own role.
_Avoid_: Firm (the derived workspace mode), account, tenant

**Admin**:
The desktop-only area, reached from the bottom of the rail, that holds every setting: Organization (Dashboard, Companies, Users) and the current Company (Configuration, Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Suppliers, Integrations). Account-level settings (security, sign out) live in the account menu, not in Admin. Admin › Dashboard is the per-company triage rollup for an organization with more than one company; it is not the workspace home.
_Avoid_: Settings (as the area's name), Controls (folded into Configuration), preferences

**Configuration**:
The Admin section that says what a company's queues and Detail pane show and what may happen without a person: the per-type field table (Editable, Required, Width), the autonomy level and what blocks a publish, tax, email intake and what is switched on. Every switch carries one sentence saying what it changes.
_Avoid_: Automation settings, workspace settings

**Immersive surface**:
A document-detail or worksheet page that temporarily takes over the viewport while preserving workspace identity, a clear return action, and relevant workspace status.

**Queue screen**:
A typed destination's list view (Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions). The queue fills the work area; selecting a row opens the Detail pane beside it, and the operator never leaves the screen to review, approve, or resolve a row.

**Detail pane**:
The single right-hand pane on a Queue screen that shows the selected row's extracted fields beside its source document, with its approval chain, audit trail, and open checks as tabs. There is one Detail pane per Queue screen; it is the only place a row's detail opens in place.

**Origin context**:
The workspace, list, filters, position, and workflow state from which a user opened a detail or action surface. Returning from that surface restores the origin context whenever it still exists.

**Workflow operation**:
An in-progress or recently completed unit of work such as extraction, sync, review assignment, worksheet placement, approval, or publish. An operation remains discoverable after navigation so the user can understand what happened and what to do next.

**Operation status**:
The user-facing progress and outcome for a workflow operation, shown inline where the operation began and in the workspace activity/status area. It includes the current step, progress when known, and a plain-language next action.

**Partial outcome**:
A batch result in which individual items may succeed, need review, be skipped, be canceled, or fail. Partial outcomes remain visible per item rather than being collapsed into one batch-level success or failure.

**Server-confirmed action**:
An action whose durable or external effect is not treated as complete until the server confirms it, including approvals, ledger pushes, and other financial writes. Local optimistic feedback may precede confirmation only for reversible, low-risk changes.

**Touchless**:
A document whose extracted fields all met the workspace's confidence threshold and was pushed to the ledger without a human review step. Shown on a record as a fact once it has happened, not as a prediction or a pending state.
_Avoid_: Auto-approved, zero-touch

**Processing state**:
Where a queue row stands in the intake → review → approval path, shown as one mark at the row's leading edge. Exactly one of, in precedence order: Cancelled, Needs attention (a check blocked it, an escalation is open, or an approval was rejected), In review, Touchless, Approved. Ledger facts such as Synced or Paid are not processing states and are shown separately. Due-date urgency is not a processing state either.
_Avoid_: Status (the column of pills is broader), aging (that is the due-date signal)

**Confidence threshold**:
The single workspace-set score an extracted field must reach to count as confident. It is the same floor Touchless is judged against, so a field that clears it in a queue row would also clear it for Touchless. A field entered by a person, or never scored by extraction, has no confidence and shows no confidence claim at all — absence means "not an AI claim", not "low".
_Avoid_: High confidence, low confidence (as if they were fixed numbers), the internal stage cutoff or amount-band floors (those are gates, not the user-facing threshold)

## Public marketing and coverage

**Supported coverage**:
A jurisdiction with a registered, working jurisdiction pack that can support the relevant document-to-ledger workflow.
_Avoid_: Global support, available everywhere

**Roadmap coverage**:
A jurisdiction the product may support later but cannot currently accept for the relevant workflow. It must not be presented as available or used to qualify a current signup promise.
_Avoid_: Supported, coming soon (unless the rollout is an explicit product commitment)

**Trial**:
A time-bounded product-access period with an explicit start, expiry, and billing or cancellation path. DocuBite must not use this term publicly until those supporting paths exist.
_Avoid_: Free workspace, evaluation

**Account creation**:
The current public entry action: creating a DocuBite account before setting up or joining a workspace. It is not a trial start or a payment event.
_Avoid_: Start free trial, Subscribe

**Workspace storage cap**:
The hard limit of 200 MB of stored documents per workspace. It must be disclosed before an upload is accepted, even when it is omitted from the marketing CTA.
_Avoid_: Unlimited storage

**Connected accounting system**:
An external accounting platform a workspace can connect to today, currently QuickBooks Online or Xero.
_Avoid_: Available integration when the connector is not live

**Built-in ledger**:
DocuBite's own double-entry ledger destination. It is a product capability, not an external integration.
_Avoid_: Third-party integration

**Planned integration**:
A named future accounting destination shown as roadmap intent, not as a capability available today. Planned integrations must not be presented with vendor marks without approved permission.
_Avoid_: Supported, connected, coming soon

**Product capability**:
A public-facing product area organized around one coherent mechanism and the visitor outcome it enables. The current capability vocabulary is Document extraction, Controls & fraud, Close the books, Data health, and Integrations & API.
_Avoid_: Feature list, module

**Product overview**:
The public entry point that orients visitors to the product capability set before directing them to detailed capability pages.
_Avoid_: Feature dump, single-scroll feature wall

**Trust & security**:
The procurement-facing explanation of DocuBite's safeguards, data handling, access controls, auditability, and compliance posture. It is a trust destination, not a Product capability.
_Avoid_: Security feature, compliance promise

**Solution**:
A role-oriented explanation of how DocuBite fits a team's workflow. Document types describe capabilities and belong with Product, not with the role-oriented Solutions structure.
_Avoid_: Document type, industry page

**Document extraction**:
The Product capability that turns supported PDFs and images into reviewable structured rows with visible confidence and source provenance. It describes the extraction and review mechanism, not a guarantee that every input is readable.
_Avoid_: Perfect OCR, quality rescue

**Controls & fraud**:
The Product capability that applies explainable checks, gates, approval rules, and human review before risky workflow steps.
_Avoid_: Fraud prevention guarantee, autonomous approval

**Close the books**:
The Product capability that coordinates close checklists, gated period transitions, accrual drafts, aging, matching, and related month-end work.
_Avoid_: Automatic close, payment execution

**Data health**:
The Product capability that surfaces scored pipeline, ledger, and tax hygiene so teams can find drift before it becomes a reconciliation problem.
_Avoid_: Data correctness guarantee, audit certification

**Integrations & API**:
The Product capability for sending reviewed data to the built-in ledger, connected accounting systems, and workspace-scoped external systems through documented API and webhook surfaces.
_Avoid_: Universal integration, available connector when it is only planned

**Capability page**:
A detailed public Product page organized around one outcome, one mechanism, evidence-backed proof points, explicit limits, and one account-creation action.
_Avoid_: Feature dump, unsupported promise

## Resolution — 2026-09-15 (autopilot)

Grilled in two rounds with `intent` (`transpose` → `journey` → `fortify` → `articulate` → `include` → `measure`), `impeccable adapt`, `grilling` and `domain-modeling`. Per the autopilot brief every question was answered with its ➡️ recommendation; the rule that decided each is on the report (`docs/wayfinder-reports/226/232.md`). Nothing here reverses a #177 decision; #189 (Approval only on the phone), #209 (cards, timeline, bar), #224 (combined pane), #227 (Approvals content), #231 (Account tab), #237 (workspace home) are cited as-is.

**Incumbent evidence, cited not re-run** (the mobile inbox is being replaced by #227 §16, so its score is evidence, not a baseline): #227's critique of `review-inbox.tsx` **21/40**, in-page 12/6 · 17/9; **P0** the mobile Approve/Reject bar paints under the tab bar (`review-inbox.tsx:750` vs `mobile-tab-bar.tsx:36`); **P1** optimistic approval; **P1** "—" amounts; **P1** a second grammar. #225's Invoices Detail sheet at 390: 6/5 pane-open. Facts checked: `User.avatar` exists (photos in the timeline when set); `Supplier` carries `documentCount`, `lastSeenAt`, `paymentTermsDays`; `lib/checks/duplicates.ts` is the near-duplicate signal; `DetailPane` is already a `fixed inset-0 z-50` sheet below `lg` and `split-pane.tsx` already stacks the source 38vh above the fields when embedded.

### Decisions

1. **Landing stays the Invoices queue on every width** (CONTEXT.md "Workspace home", #237). Vic's two-card home is not adopted: it is an overview surface, costs a tap, and its one virtue (the empty queue stays present) is delivered by decision 4. No viewport-sniffing redirect.
2. **Phone tab bar: Approvals · Invoices · Exceptions · Account.** Approvals leads because the phone is the Approver's lane (#239 Q7); Account per #231. Finance and Archive leave the bar (#239: off the daily route / lookup side-path) and live as an "Also in this workspace" list on the Account screen with Purchase Orders, Receipts and Bank Statements — all read-only, content-only when deep-linked. Badges: Approvals = my Ready to Approve count (#227 §9), Exceptions = open count; **Invoices loses its badge** (workspace-wide review work is not the phone's lane — Attention Bait, cat. 5).
3. **Empty Approvals** = the "done" state: "Nothing needs your approval", "N waiting on other approvers" with the `Approver · Anyone` chip, link to Invoices. Never a dead end.
4. **One list screen, Ready to Approve**, with a segmented control **Invoices (n) · PO Mismatches (n)** — both counts always present, even at zero. Sort + facets collapse into one **Filter** button opening a bottom sheet (#225 evidence: chips wrap to three rows at 390).
5. **Row = card, ≥64px**, processing mark leading (#223): Supplier · Amount (tabular, ink not green) / Invoice # · Due / Stage ("2 of 3 · Owner sign-off") or the **Not eligible** reason pill. PO Mismatches: PO # · Variance (amount, %) on line 2. **No checkboxes below `lg` — bulk is desktop-only**; one row, one decision (Destructive Defaults, cat. 9).
6. **One sheet, not Vic's two screens.** The below-`lg` Detail pane is the phone screen: source strip (38vh, collapsible to "Show source") over tabs **Approval · Details · Checks · History**, opening on Approval, fields read-only while a stage is pending (#227 §6). Vic's "View → Approval Context" is the source strip expanding. CONTEXT.md's Detail pane entry now says so and lists "Approval Context" under _Avoid_.
7. **Timeline: one component on both widths** — vertical, a node per stage (decided: name · when · reason; current: "Waiting on you" / "Waiting on ‹name›"; not reached), INITIATED as the first node, avatar from `User.avatar` or initials. This is #227 §6's STEP n list in the tour's form; #209's mobile build is the starting point.
8. **"From this supplier" on the Approval tab, both widths, no new model**: invoice count, last seen, terms (#229's "2/10 net 30" when set), and the near-duplicate check as "Possible duplicate of ‹#› · ‹state›" when it fired. Graduates the "More From This Vendor" fog.
9. **PO Mismatches on the phone**: Approve = `overrideGate(reason)` with the reason sheet; the variance summary (#228's Ordered · Already invoiced · This invoice · Allowance · Over by) shown read-only; "Match lines on desktop" as a note. Per-cell glyphs stay desktop (#189, #228).
10. **Decision bar**: sticky sheet footer, **Reject (outline) · Approve (filled emerald)**, equal halves, 48px, safe-area padding; the sheet stacks above the tab bar (`z-50` over `z-40`) so the bar is bottom-most — the P0 is fixed by construction. Reject → bottom sheet with the required reason; Approve → #185's count-bearing modal as a bottom sheet with optional comment. No swipe gestures, no single-tap approve.
11. **After a decision the Approver stays on the row** (#239): "Approving…" (disabled, Server-confirmed), then the result inline with **Next to approve** and **Back to list**. No auto-advance.
12. **History**: below `lg`, opening a row pushes history so the system Back closes the sheet; ↑/↓ inside the sheet replace. Desktop keeps `replaceState`.
13. **State inventory** (execution checklist, from #227 §10 with phone rendering): offline → buttons disabled with "You're offline — decisions need a connection", list readable · server refused → inline "Approved by ‹name› ‹ago›", row refreshes · Not eligible → Approve disabled with the reason as visible text above the bar, Reject enabled · loading → 64px card skeletons · nothing for me · nothing for me but pending on others · ineligible only · partial (n/a — no bulk) · no workflow · approver no longer a member.
14. **Words**: tab "Approvals"; screen title "Ready to Approve"; sheet title supplier, subtitle invoice # · amount; "Waiting on you" not "In Progress" (#233); reasons in plain words.
15. **Rendering at 390**: card title 15px/600, secondary 13px slate-600 (≥4.5:1), `tabular-nums`, inputs 16px, 16px gutters, hairlines slate-200; emerald only on the primary action and the current node, red only on Reject and rejected nodes. Sheet slides in 200ms ease-out, instant under `prefers-reduced-motion`; result crossfades 150ms.
16. **Accessibility**: sheet `role="dialog" aria-modal`, focus to heading on open, Back first in tab order, footer reachable by Tab, segmented control as `tablist`, result in `aria-live="polite"`, 48px targets, no colour-only state.
17. **Tablet band (`md`–`lg`)** unchanged: rail carries Approvals, sheet is full-screen. Tab-bar decisions are `<md`; sheet decisions are `<lg`.
18. **Measure** (recorded, not instrumented): share of decisions below `lg`; Start → decision time; counter-metrics: reject-then-cancel and modal-dismiss rates, decisions/minute not spiking.

### Action Summary for the execution ticket (in order)

Intent: `specify` (spec + copy matrix + test plan from the decisions above) → `fortify` (decision 13's inventory in code before the happy path is called done) → `articulate` (decision 14) → `include` (decision 16).
Impeccable: `adapt` (tab bar, card list, segmented control, Filter sheet, sheet over the tab bar, pushState) → `layout` (card anatomy, timeline, "From this supplier") → `clarify` → `harden` (offline, refused, Not eligible) → `animate` (decision 15's motion) → `audit` → `polish`.
Definition of done: in-page `detect.js` on `/approvals/invoices` and `/approvals/po-mismatches` at 1440 and 390, list and sheet-open, before/after counts; critique on the new UI at ≥3/4 per heuristic; `evaluate` ≥80 with every heuristic ≥1; `craft-floor.md` read before the first edit if it exists (it does not today — #236 flagged it).

Execution: **#{{EXEC}}**. Input posted to #235 (the queue's below-`md` rendering): the phone card anatomy here is the evidence that approval-on-a-phone favours the card row.

## Destination

DocuBite's authenticated app works the way Vic.ai's does, end to end: **Vic's interaction grammar, DocuBite's skin.** Every operator surface — Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Approvals (Invoices / PO Mismatches), Bill Pay, Payment Batches, and Admin — shares one shell: a full-width 62px queue, one header band (View · Sort · summary filter chips opening a hierarchical facet panel), a bulk action row, and one right-hand Detail pane with a sticky bottom action bar. PO mismatches are resolved on the invoice row with per-cell match glyphs and the tolerance arithmetic in view. Payment runs are batched, approved and exported without DocuBite moving money. Admin is a distinct area (Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies) with multi-company access. Approval works on a phone. Implemented and shipped, measured by Impeccable's in-page detector and a critique score above the 20/40 baseline on every queue.

Evidence: the full self-guided tour walked 2026-09-15 — `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (DocuBite's own Invoices screen from the same day sits beside them).

## Notes

**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.

**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.

**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.

**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.

**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.

**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.

**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**

- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.

## Decisions so far

<!-- one line per closed ticket -->
- #230 (research): Workspace is already the Company (71/80 models keyed on workspaceId, one Bigcapital org per workspace, nothing above it); one login/many companies already works via per-workspace `WorkspaceMember.role`, the grouping is what is missing; both isolation layers key on `workspace_id`, so Companies should be an additive `Organization` + nullable `Workspace.organizationId` + `OrganizationMember`, with `WorkspaceMember` the only grant of entity access — [docs/research/multi-company-access.md](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/blob/research/multi-company-access/docs/research/multi-company-access.md); eight open decisions handed to #231.

- [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225) (task, shipped): the Queue screen is live on Invoices / POs / Receipts / Bank Statements / Exceptions — full-width 62px queue, one header band with facet chips, 60% right Detail pane with ↑/↓/Esc + sticky Approve/Reject, 56px icon rail, deep links; aging totals moved to the Dashboard as "Open invoices by age". In-page detector Invoices 30/26 · 41/34 → 6/5 · 6/5; critique 20/40 → 25/40. Critique findings with a decision became [#233](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/233) (one status vocabulary), [#234](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/234) (pane header stack), [#235](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/235) (below-md rendering — reopens a #224 choice, loop budget 1 of 2); the leading-glyph finding went to #223.

## Destination

DocuBite's authenticated app works the way Vic.ai's does, end to end: **Vic's interaction grammar, DocuBite's skin.** Every operator surface — Invoices, Purchase Orders, Receipts, Bank Statements, Exceptions, Approvals (Invoices / PO Mismatches), Bill Pay, Payment Batches, and Admin — shares one shell: a full-width 62px queue, one header band (View · Sort · summary filter chips opening a hierarchical facet panel), a bulk action row, and one right-hand Detail pane with a sticky bottom action bar. PO mismatches are resolved on the invoice row with per-cell match glyphs and the tolerance arithmetic in view. Payment runs are batched, approved and exported without DocuBite moving money. Admin is a distinct area (Configuration, Approval Flows, Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies) with multi-company access. Approval works on a phone. Implemented and shipped, measured by Impeccable's in-page detector and a critique score above the 20/40 baseline on every queue.

Evidence: the full self-guided tour walked 2026-09-15 — `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots in `docs/vic-ai-tour-2026-09-15/` (DocuBite's own Invoices screen from the same day sits beside them).

## Notes

**Supersedes [Map: Vic.ai-style typed AP surfaces (#177)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/177).** #177's thirty closed decisions are this map's baseline and are cited, not re-decided. Its two open tickets, [Build the five-state processing glyph (#223)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/223) and [Build the typed list-screen composition on all five queues (#225)](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/225), are re-parented here. #177 is closed.

**Why a second map.** #177 reached its destination as feature slices bolted onto the old pages, with no ticket owning composition and no in-browser verification, and scored 20/40 ([#224](https://github.com/petrose99/docubite/issues/224)). This map charts by *surface*, each ticket owning a whole screen's shape, and every execution ticket closes on detector counts.

**Execution mode.** This map carries execution. Decision tickets resolve first; each spawns an execution ticket; execution tickets close only with `impeccable` run at the four points in CLAUDE.md, in-page detector before/after counts at 1440 and 390 (list and pane-open), and `polish`. Dev-server + seed + headless-Chromium recipe is on #225.

**Design protocol.** Every rendered-surface ticket calls the Skill tool for `impeccable` (sub-command named on the ticket) and `intent`, before the work. Grilling tickets on a surface open with `impeccable critique` of the incumbent and cite the tour screenshot they are matching.

**Vic wins ties, with the tour as the record.** "Does this follow Vic or DocuBite?" defaults to Vic without asking, and the answer is read off `docs/vic-ai-ux-tour-findings.md` §6 and the screenshots — not from memory of the older sections. Grill only what the tour does not settle: DocuBite-only features (Exceptions, Touchless, does-not-move-money, bank statements, institutions), data DocuBite lacks (payment terms, discounts, buyers, entities), and anything that would reverse a #177 decision.

**Documented exceptions to Vic** (decided, do not re-open by "Vic wins ties"): the combined fields+source Detail pane (#179 → #224) with History as its tabs instead of Vic's left panel; the collapsible icon rail instead of Vic's top bar (#224 Q5); DocuBite's palette, type and emerald brand (this map, Q2); Exceptions as its own destination (#192); Touchless keeps its name.

**Settled while charting (grilled 2026-09-15):**

- **Scope is the whole operator app** — queues + Detail pane, Approvals inbox, PO matching in the row, Bill Pay + Payment Batches, Admin, mobile approval. One grammar everywhere.
- **Fidelity is grammar, not skin.** Same layouts, panels, chips, bars, keyboard flow, copy patterns; colour and type stay DocuBite's.
- **Payments never move money.** Bill Pay queue (open bills, terms, countdown, discounted amount over struck-through due) and Payment Batches queue (batch → approve → export file). The transfer stays outside DocuBite, as `preparePaymentRun` does today.
- **Approvals is a destination with two queues**, Invoices and PO Mismatches, each a personal Ready-to-Approve view with the sticky Approve/Reject bar. Exceptions stays separate.
- **Admin adopts Vic's full IA including Companies**: Configuration (per-field Editable/Required/Width, consequence toggles), Approval Flows, PO Mismatch Flows, Users, Companies — one login, many companies, per-entity permissions. This is the one schema-and-auth effort on the map; it is researched before it is grilled.
- **Build order:** shell (#225) → distill (#238) → Approvals → PO matching → Payments → Admin → Mobile.
- **Removal protocol (owner's rule, #237):** nothing is removed from the app without the owner signing off each removal by name on the ticket. Removed features are *unplugged* (CONTEXT.md term), not deleted, so a return is a re-link.
